$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=7x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=7y(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(-3) \\ y(-3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7t} & t{e}^{7t} \\ 0 & {e}^{7t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}].$*

worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c,
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t+3)}\,x(-3) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{7(t+3)} & (t+3){e}^{7(t+3)} \\ 0 & {e}^{7(t+3)}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\,(-2t-6){e}^{7(t+3)}\, \\ \,-2{e}^{7(t+3)}\,\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Given the system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=Φ(t)c, where Φ(t) is a fundamental matrix of the system, and c is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as x(t)=Φ0(t)c=eAtc, where Φ0(t)=eAt is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting t=t0, we have x(t0)=eAt0c, and since eAt is invertible for all t, we have c=e−At0x(t0).

Plugging the above back into our expression for x(t), we get x(t)=eAte−At0x(t0)=eA(t−t0)x(t0).
